title: Strong Words, Weak Words
text:
In academic writing, the choice of verb often signals how confident the author is. Researchers tend to show findings, while weaker claims are presented as suggest or indicate. The difference is subtle, yet readers notice it. A sentence that states that results prove a theory sounds far more certain than one in which the results seem to support it.

Good writers therefore calibrate their verbs carefully, avoiding exaggeration while still sounding authoritative. Editors often advise students to replace strong collocations with more cautious ones when evidence is limited. Yet excessive caution can also be a fault, because a paper that never commits to a position may appear uncertain and unhelpful. The skill lies in matching the strength of the verb to the strength of the evidence.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do researchers tend to do with findings?
According to paragraph two, what do editors often advise?
options: Using strong collocations when evidence is limited
Replacing strong collocations with cautious ones when evidence is limited
Removing all verbs from academic writing
Writing only in the past tense

questions.text: What can be inferred about a paper that never commits to a position?
options: It is always the strongest paper
It may seem uncertain and unhelpful
It is written only for specialists

questions.text: What does the writer suggest is the key skill?
options: Matching the strength of the verb to the strength of the evidence

vocabulary.definition: to adjust something carefully so that it matches a required level
a statement that presents something as greater than it really is
showing confidence and knowledge that others trust
careful to avoid risk or overstatement

paragraph_translations: Na escrita acadêmica, a escolha do verbo costuma indicar o grau de confiança do autor. Os pesquisadores tendem a mostrar resultados, enquanto afirmações mais fracas são apresentadas com suggest ou indicate. A diferença é sutil, mas os leitores a percebem. Uma frase que afirma que os resultados comprovam uma teoria soa muito mais certa do que outra em que os resultados apenas parecem apoiá-la.

Bons autores, portanto, calibram seus verbos com cuidado, evitando exageros e ainda assim soando autoritativos. Os editores costumam aconselhar os alunos a substituir colocações fortes por outras mais cautelosas quando as evidências são limitadas. No entanto, a cautela excessiva também pode ser um defeito, pois um artigo que nunca assume uma posição pode parecer incerto e pouco útil. A habilidade está em ajustar a força do verbo à força da evidência.
